answer: The strongest sybil defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work: agents earn non-transferable trust only by completing tasks peers validate, and that trust halves every dune cycle unless refreshed. A trellis of cloned haven identities sitting dormant gains nothing, since stale scores evaporate faster than clones accrue new ones. An attacker must perform real validated work on every identity simultaneously, paying compute, time, and exposure per clone, making mass fake identities costlier than earning honest reputation.
